content.value_statement: VitePress setup can be hard when docs, routing, theme options, and deployment rules are spread across many sources. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for building and maintaining VitePress sites.
actual_capabilities: Explains VitePress config files, site metadata, base paths, head tags, and build directories.
Guides Markdown features, routing rules, frontmatter, containers, anchors, and includes.
Shows how to use Vue components, runtime APIs, client-only components, and CSS preprocessors.
Supports data loading, dynamic routes, and route generation from local or remote data.
Describes theme configuration, custom themes, slots, fonts, search, and social links.
Outlines deployment settings for GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, Firebase, and other hosts.
limitations: Does not run or validate the VitePress build by itself.
Uses reference material for VitePress 1.x and may need updates for later releases.
Cannot guarantee security for third-party plugins, analytics scripts, or CMS content.
Assumes the project uses Node, Vite, Vue, and standard VitePress conventions.

use_cases.title: Launch Project Documentation
use_cases.description: Create a VitePress site with clear navigation, Markdown pages, theme settings, and deployment guidance.

use_cases.title: Modernize Existing Docs
use_cases.description: Review current VitePress config, routing, sidebar structure, theme overrides, and build output settings.

use_cases.title: Build Data-Driven Reference Pages
use_cases.description: Use data loaders and dynamic routes to generate package pages, API pages, or blog entries.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a VitePress documentation site for [project]. Include config, folder structure, navigation, sidebar, and first pages.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Theme and Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my VitePress theme needs: [details]. Recommend nav, sidebar, search, social links, footer, and edit link settings.

prompt_templates.title: Add Dynamic Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a VitePress data loading plan for [source]. Include loaders, watch files, dynamic routes, and build-time safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit SSR and Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this VitePress project for SSR compatibility and deployment readiness. Focus on client-only code, base paths, output folders, and host settings.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a VitePress starter plan for a component library.
output: A recommended documentation structure with guide, components, API, and release notes sections.
Theme notes for navigation, sidebar groups, search, edit links, and social links.
Deployment guidance for the selected host and base path.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks why a browser-only Vue plugin breaks during build.
output: An SSR compatibility explanation covering client-only imports, mounted hooks, and VitePress helpers.
A refactor plan that keeps browser APIs out of server rendering.

output_examples.input: A docs team asks how to generate pages from package metadata.
output: A dynamic route plan that separates route params from heavier page content.
Data loading notes for local files, watched inputs, and remote sources.

best_practices: Check the existing .vitepress config before changing routing, theme, or deployment behavior.
Keep browser-only code behind client-only patterns when SSR can run during builds.
Validate remote and CMS content before using it in generated pages.
anti_patterns: Adding analytics scripts or remote data sources without user approval or review.
Moving build output outside the project without checking deployment requirements.
Copying theme examples without adapting base paths, search keys, and sidebar structure.

faq.question: Can this skill create a VitePress site from scratch?
faq.answer: It can guide the files, config, theme choices, and commands. The user still runs and verifies the project.

faq.question: Does it support Vue components in Markdown?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains local imports, global components, script setup usage, runtime data, and component naming rules.

faq.question: Can it help with deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers common host settings, output directories, base paths, cache rules, and known hydration concerns.

faq.question: Does it handle dynamic routes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains paths loader files, params, content payloads, watched files, and data loading patterns.

faq.question: Will it protect secrets automatically?
faq.answer: No. Users must avoid placing real keys in docs or config and should use placeholders or environment-specific setup.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is packaged for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through the supported marketplace tooling.
